claims.text: Corrosion-related degradation in pre-exposure Q235 steel begins through formation of a corrosive microenvironment at the steel surface.
Elevated temperature accelerates formation of the corrosive surface microenvironment.
Increasing environmental harshness accelerates formation of the corrosive surface microenvironment.
Oxidation contributes to corrosion of Q235 steel under the proposed exposure conditions.
Electrochemical reactions contribute to corrosion of Q235 steel under the proposed exposure conditions.
The corrosion rate and degradation of Q235 steel increase as temperature increases.
The corrosion rate and degradation of Q235 steel increase as environmental harshness increases.
The proposed hypothesis applies from room temperature to 500°C and from dry to highly corrosive environments.
The exact corrosion mechanisms and effects of environmental factors on Q235 steel are not fully understood.
Q235 samples should be compared across controlled temperatures and environments using corrosion-rate, microstructural, and electrochemical measurements.
Failure of corrosion rate to increase with increasing temperature and environmental harshness would falsify the hypothesis.
